sponsors: Rep. Justin Slaughter and House co-sponsors; Senate sponsors Lakesia Collins and Doris Turner
status: Passed House 114-1-0 on 2025-04-10; arrived in Senate, assigned to Executive Committee, deadline extended, then re-referred to Senate Assignments Committee (Rule 3-9(a)) 2025-06-02; no action recorded since
key_provisions: Requires state data storage contracts to keep data in the United States and creates bid credits for Illinois and opportunity-zone storage, including data center-related provisions.

status: Filed 2026-01-07; first reading and referred to House Rules Committee 2026-01-14; no further action recorded
key_provisions: Creates a compensation framework for property owners within 1,000 feet of a data center for value loss, business revenue loss, or adverse impacts such as noise, vibration, traffic, stormwater burden, or lighting; limits concurrent home-rule powers.

bill: HB5513 (Hyperscale Data Centers / POWER Act companion)
sponsors: Rep. Robyn Gabel with multiple House Democratic co-sponsors
status: Assigned to Executive Committee 2026-02-24; re-referred to House Rules Committee (Rule 19(a)) 2026-03-27; co-sponsors continued to be added through 2026-05-27 with no further procedural action
key_provisions: House companion to SB4016 with environmental, water, energy, public-benefit, reporting, and solar permitting provisions.

sponsors: Sen. Sue Rezin; co-sponsors Sally J. Turner and Terri Bryant
status: Referred to Senate Assignments Committee 2025-01-17; co-sponsors added 2025-04-03; no action recorded in 2026
key_provisions: Confirmed via ILGA synopsis: creates the Data Center Construction by Foreign Adversaries Act; bars a foreign-adversary-controlled company from constructing a data center in Illinois unless ICC, IPA, and DCEO jointly certify load conditions.

status: Moved to Executive Committee 2026-01-27; to AI and Social Media Committee 2026-02-04; amendment filed 2026-03-31; committee deadline chain extended 2026-03-27 to 2026-04-24 to 2026-05-15 to 2026-05-22; bill and amendment re-referred to Senate Assignments Committee (Rule 3-9(a)) 2026-05-22
key_provisions: Creates Illinois Data Center Energy and Water Reporting Act; annual energy and water reporting to IPA; IPA ratepayer-impact study; confidentiality, public access, enforcement, and penalties.

sponsors: Sen. Mark L. Walker; co-sponsors Chris Balkema and Robert Peters
status: Assigned to Senate Revenue Committee 2025-03-04; committee/3rd reading deadline extended to 2025-06-01; re-referred to Senate Assignments Committee (Rule 3-9(a)) 2025-06-02; no action recorded in 2026
key_provisions: Expands the state data center definition for incentive purposes to include a quantum research facility.

status: To AI and Social Media Committee 2026-02-18; committee deadline chain extended 2026-03-27 to 2026-04-24 to 2026-05-15 to 2026-05-22; re-referred to Senate Assignments Committee (Rule 3-9(a)) 2026-05-22
key_provisions: Conditions data center incentive qualification on water stewardship strategy disclosure and requires DCEO reporting on recipient water stewardship strategies.

status: To AI and Social Media Committee 2026-02-25; Rule 2-10 deadline chain extended 2026-03-27 to 2026-04-24 to 2026-05-15 to 2026-05-22; re-referred to Senate Assignments Committee (Rule 3-9(a)) 2026-05-22
key_provisions: Establishes data center self-direct clean energy program, 180-day preconstruction disclosure to ICC, public meeting requirements, water-use disclosures to DNR, penalties up to $10,000 per violation, and utility tariff review.

status: To AI and Social Media Committee 2026-02-25; Amendment No. 2 filed 2026-04-27; Rule 2-10 deadline chain extended 2026-03-27 to 2026-04-24 to 2026-05-15 to 2026-05-22; bill and both amendments re-referred to Senate Assignments Committee (Rule 3-9(a)) 2026-05-22
key_provisions: Similar clean energy self-direct and utility tariff framework; adds water discharge pollutant identification, DNR water-use disclosure, Water Use Act changes, and groundwater emergency provisions.

status: To AI and Social Media Committee 2026-02-25; Rule 2-10 deadline chain extended 2026-03-27 to 2026-04-24 to 2026-05-15 to 2026-05-22; Senate Committee Amendment No. 1 filed 2026-05-05; bill and amendment re-referred to Senate Assignments Committee (Rule 3-9(a)) 2026-05-22; co-sponsors added through 2026-06-17
key_provisions: Creates Data Center Water Transparency and Aquifer Protection Act; bars data centers from using Mahomet Aquifer water beginning 2027; bars permits for Mahomet withdrawals; requires existing users to transition by 2028; bans local nondisclosure clauses restricting water-use disclosure.

sponsors: Sen. Ram Villivalam with chief co-sponsors Robert Peters, Graciela Guzman, and Rachel Ventura, plus additional co-sponsors
status: To AI and Social Media Committee 2026-02-25; Rule 2-10 deadline chain extended 2026-03-27 to 2026-04-24 to 2026-05-15 to 2026-05-22; re-referred to Senate Assignments Committee (Rule 3-9(a)) 2026-05-22; co-sponsors added through 2026-05-30
key_provisions: Comprehensive hyperscale data center regulation: cumulative impact review, public notice, community benefit agreements, NDA restrictions, water-impact permits, quarterly water reporting, water scarcity plans, energy and water reporting to ICC, hyperscale self-direct program, funds supported by annual fees based on peak demand, labor and equity provisions.

status: Reported by House Technology and Innovation Committee on 2026-06-10; awaiting House floor vote as of 2026-07-31.
key_provisions: Ohio Right to Compute Act; limits state and local restrictions on computational resources, with AI risk-management requirements and nuisance language tied to physical infrastructure.

status: Passed House 97-0 on 2026-03-18; Senate Energy Committee reported and then recommitted the bill to itself on 2026-06-10; no further Senate action as of 2026-07-31.
key_provisions: Creates Data Center Study Commission to study environmental impacts, grid and rate effects, water and wastewater, noise, light, local economy, farmland, national security, and opposition messaging; report due within six months if enacted.

status: Introduced 2026-02-12; referred to House Local Government Committee on 2026-02-18; no further action as of 2026-07-31.
key_provisions: Prohibits certain county, township, and village officials from entering nondisclosure agreements; response to data center secrecy concerns but not data-center-specific in title.

status: Introduced 2026-02-17; referred to House Energy Committee on 2026-02-25 (packet-reported first hearing 2026-03-04 not independently verified on status page); no further action as of 2026-07-31.
key_provisions: Imposes minimum requirements on data center customers; minimum 12-year contract commitments, exit payments, unused capacity charges, and financial assurances so grid costs are not shifted to other customers.

status: Introduced 2026-02-24; referred to House General Government Committee on 2026-02-25; no further action as of 2026-07-31.
key_provisions: Prohibits public support for, and limits construction of, new data centers; restricts subsidies and siting near certain sensitive lands and requires developer cost responsibility.

party: D; D [VERIFY: party of Crystal Lett confirmed as D via legislative records; both sponsors are central Ohio Democrats]
status: Introduced 2026-03-24; referred to House Energy Committee on 2026-03-25; no further action as of 2026-07-31.
key_provisions: Requires monthly and yearly data center water consumption reporting and prohibits data center water-use information in nondisclosure agreements with political subdivisions.

status: Signed by Governor with line-item veto on 2025-06-30; veto preserved the ORC 122.175 data center sales/use tax exemption; operating appropriations effective 2025-06-30.
key_provisions: Budget bill amended ORC 122.175 computer data center sales and use tax exemption framework; veto blocked repeal of the exemption.

status: Introduced 2025-03-12; referred to Senate Housing Committee on 2025-03-19; no further action as of 2026-07-31.
key_provisions: Broad development/housing package amending ORC 122.175 and related data center tax-exemption language.

sponsors: Louis W. Blessing III; Kent Smith
status: Introduced 2025-05-06; referred to Senate Finance Committee on 2025-05-07; no further action as of 2026-07-31.
key_provisions: Tax package amending ORC 122.175 data center exemption mechanics, definitions, compliance, and reporting.

sponsors: Louis W. Blessing III; Kent Smith
status: Introduced 2026-03-11; referred to Senate Finance Committee on 2026-03-25; no further action as of 2026-07-31.
key_provisions: Prohibits new data center sales and use tax exemptions after a specified date, reported as 2027-10-01.

sponsors: Willis E. Blackshear Jr.; Casey Weinstein
status: Introduced 2026-03-16; referred to Senate Public Utilities Committee on 2026-03-25; no further action as of 2026-07-31.
key_provisions: Responsible Water Use by Data Centers Act; requires data centers to pay attributable water/sewer infrastructure costs, creates water-use permitting/reporting, and bars permits for new or increased consumptive use over 5 million gallons per day averaged over 30 days.

status: Introduced 2026-03-19; referred to Senate Public Utilities Committee on 2026-03-25; no further action as of 2026-07-31.
key_provisions: Requires PUCO approval of agreements to interconnect data centers to the electrical grid; cosponsors include Willis Blackshear, Hearcel Craig, Bill DeMora, and Kent Smith.
